literal_edits.source_excerpt: 1.1 On a mesh cell centered at $m_i$, write $s=t-m_i$. Taylor's formula gives $u_*'(m_i+s)=u_*'(m_i)+s u_*''(m_i)+r(s)$ with $\|r(s)\|_2\le M_3s^2/2$. Averaging over the symmetric interval cancels the odd term and gives $\|(u_*(t_{i+1})-u_*(t_i))/h-u_*'(m_i)\|_2\le M_3h^2/24$. The average endpoint state differs from $u_*(m_i)$ by at most $M_2h^2/8$, so the Lipschitz bound $L_f$ gives $\|G_h(Y^*)\|_\infty\le C_0h^2$; the boundary residual is exactly zero. These are uniform cellwise bounds, hence independent of the number of cells. [F1, F4, given, algebra]
literal_edits.proposed_replacement: 1.1 On a mesh cell centered at $m_i$, repeated vector FTC gives $u_*'(m_i+s)=u_*'(m_i)+s u_*''(m_i)+r(s)$, where $r(s)=\int_0^s\int_0^v u_*'''(m_i+w)\,dw\,dv$. For negative limits reverse their orientation before applying the norm inequality. Thus $\|r(s)\|_2\le M_3|s|^2/2$. Averaging over $[-h/2,h/2]$ cancels the odd term and gives a difference-quotient defect at most $M_3h^2/24$. Applying the same integral argument to $u_*$ at $m_i\pm h/2$ bounds each first-order remainder by $M_2h^2/8$; their average therefore bounds the endpoint-average displacement from $u_*(m_i)$ by $M_2h^2/8$. Integrating $D\widetilde f$ on the connecting segment bounds the corresponding field difference by $L_fM_2h^2/8$. The affine boundary residual is zero. Taking the maximum of the cell bounds gives $\|G_h(Y^*)\|_\infty\le C_0h^2$. [F1, F4, given, algebra]

literal_edits.proposed_replacement: 5.1 Linear interpolation is a convex combination, so $\|P_h(Y-Y_h)\|_\infty\le\|Y-Y_h\|_\infty$. On a cell $[a,b]$ of length $h$, repeated FTC gives $u_*(t)-P_hY^*(t)=-\int_a^b K_t(s)u_*''(s)\,ds$, where $K_t(s)=(b-t)(s-a)/h$ for $s\le t$ and $K_t(s)=(t-a)(b-s)/h$ for $s\ge t$. This kernel is nonnegative and has integral $(t-a)(b-t)/2\le h^2/8$, so [F4] gives the interpolation bound $M_2h^2/8$. The sample error of $Y_h$ is at most $2KC_0h^2$ by step 2.1. Combining these bounds with step 4.1 proves the displayed estimate. [F4, step 2.1, step 4.1, given, algebra] ∎

Suppose the initialization and stepper algorithms in [[alg-index-one-dae-consistent-initialization]], [[alg-index-one-dae-backward-euler-stepper]], and [[alg-index-one-dae-bdf2-stepper]] are run with finite grid length and finite Newton budget $B$. Each call returns a status after finitely many residual evaluations. A Newton call makes at most $B+1$ residual evaluations. Initialization and a time-step wrapper may each make one additional residual evaluation after a root status to record the returned residual norm or unscaled blocks, so initialization uses at most $B+2$ evaluations and a stepper with $S$ attempted steps uses at most $S(B+2)$ evaluations before returning a failure status or completed. This is a termination statement only; it does not assert that any residual tolerance is attained.

2.2 A stepper attempts a finite number $S$ of steps.
